summary: Rework pass fixing all 6 blocking faults design-critique.md's first pass found, plus the 4 non-blocking issues it asked to fold in, by re-editing the same temporary debug harness, rebuilding, and re-capturing all six frames plus recompositing the sheet -- no spec changes needed, matching critique's own diagnosis that every fault was a render/composite deviation from design-spec.md, not a flaw in it. Fixes, each verified after re-capture (not just assumed from the code change), not just applied: (1) Chrome-scale mismatch -- rewrote the compositing script (composite_sheet2.py) so every sheet-chrome value (font sizes, column/row gutters, margins, line pitches) is multiplied by the device frames' own 1260px/440pt = 2.864 px-per-point scale factor instead of being drawn at literal point-as-pixel; column/row gutters are now both 69px (previously 25px column / 34px row), and a full-resolution crop of the rebuilt sheet's chrome block confirms the column heading now reads as a heading with zero clipping or overlap at any zoom level. (2) Added an opaque #120D08 toolbar background (an explicit full-opacity color, not Theme.navBg's own 0.97-opacity token, after a first attempt at 0.97 still let a faint ghost of scrolled text bleed through on close inspection) to Option A's ScrollView-under-toolbar structure, verified via a pixel crop of the toolbar region showing zero text bleed-through. (3) Extended the debug note body to 5 paragraphs (title/date/opening paragraph held byte-identical) so Option A's secondary (top-of-note) capture now genuinely shows the reply section below the fold -- verified by re-viewing the captured frame directly. (4) Rewrote the shared reply-card view so the body Text is a direct sibling of the avatar/header HStack inside one leading VStack (previously nested in a trailing VStack that started after the avatar), flush at the card's own leading padding edge -- verified in all six re-captured frames. (5) Root-caused Option C's undersized chip: a raw (non-Button) toolbar .principal item was being squeezed by the nav bar's title-slot sizing to ~29pt tall regardless of its own .frame(height:44) request; fixed by wrapping the chip in a real Button and moving it into the trailing ToolbarItemGroup ahead of Edit, which picks up the same automatic system toolbar-button chrome Close/Edit already get -- re-measured via pixel bounding-box scan post-fix at ~55x44pt (Close/Edit measured ~44pt tall the same way, confirming parity), with real 'J'/'M' monogram letters replacing the two featureless discs. A real regression surfaced and fixed mid-pass: grouping the chip and Edit into one ToolbarItemGroup caused Edit's label to wrap onto two lines ('Edi/t') because gradientPill (unlike ghostPill) lacked the .fixedSize() call that keeps toolbar-item text single-line under a narrowed layout proposal -- added it, rebuilt, and re-verified Edit renders on one line again. (6) Fixed both baseline-drift components: captured all six frames in one continuous session with the simulator's status bar locked via `xcrun simctl status_bar override --time 9:28` (all six now read 9:28, confirmed by direct inspection), and restyled Option C's back affordance as a ghostPill-visual-language chevron + 'Note' capsule (was a bare chevron + 'Close', which also collided semantically with the parent sheet's own Close). Non-blocking items folded in per critique's explicit ask: (7) reply cards inside Option B's sheet use a 0.97-opacity cardBg variant (vs. the standard 0.90) for stronger separation against the flat #151009 sheet ground; (8) Option B's monogram stagger widened so J/M/C are all independently legible; (9) added a touch of extra manual dim behind Option B's raised sheet (on top of the system's own real dim) so A-top and B-top read as distinguishable states at thumbnail scale; (10) added a one-line Playfair title above the grid. Mechanically: re-edited FellowScript/FellowScript/FellowScript/_TempReplyVariantsDebug.swift (same temp file from the first pass, not a new one) and the same temporary FellowScriptApp.swift root-switch hook, rebuilt the FellowScript target for the iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 26.5) simulator (BUILD SUCCEEDED both after the fix-and-rebuild cycle and after final cleanup), captured all six frames in one continuous `simctl launch` + `simctl io screenshot` session per the status-bar-lock note above, resized the native 1320x2868 captures to the spec's locked 1260x2736, and recomposited the sheet with the corrected script. Cleanup, verified not just performed: _TempReplyVariantsDebug.swift deleted outright (new file, not a modification to shipped code); FellowScriptApp.swift restored from the pre-edit backup taken at the start of this pass and confirmed byte-identical via matching MD5 checksums (5abdf82c1c9c677b6e175c8b680d7e6c, the same value the first generation pass recorded); a repo-wide grep for TEMP-GEN-STEP4/ReplyVariantDebugRoot/_TempReplyVariantsDebug/REPLY_VARIANT returns zero matches; a final clean Debug build for the same simulator destination succeeded after the removal; and `git status --short` shows the exact same pre-existing, task-unrelated baseline the first generation pass already recorded (no new diffs from this session). The simulator's status bar override was cleared (`simctl status_bar clear`) after the final capture so it doesn't leak into any unrelated session.
notes: Issue 9's fix (extra manual dim behind Option B's sheet) is a real, deliberate deviation from the palette table's literal 'fixed constant, not per-option variable' framing for cardBg/ground tokens -- critique.md itself proposed both fixes 7 and 9 as sanctioned non-blocking asks, not a spec violation invented unprompted.

The sample note body (Components -> B content aside) was extended from what the first generation pass rendered -- the original longer text no longer exists (the prior pass's temp file was deleted per its own cleanup step, as required), so this pass wrote a fresh 5-paragraph body rather than attempting to reconstruct byte-identical prior wording; the deliverable's own hard constraint (identical content across all three columns within THIS pass) still holds, since all six re-captured frames share the one new body verbatim.

Frame dimensions: captured natively at 1320x2868 (iPhone 17 Pro Max's real resolution, 3x device scale) then resized to the design-spec's locked 1260x2736, consistent with the first generation pass's own convention.

Close/Edit's own real rendered extent (measured via the same pixel bounding-box method used to verify the chip) turned out to be ~44pt tall in this iOS 26 Liquid Glass toolbar despite their own compact:true code path requesting only a 32pt frame height -- the system's automatic toolbar-button chrome inflates Button-wrapped toolbar items to a shared minimum regardless of the requested frame, which is what critique.md's own '~43pt of measured outer extent' finding for Close/Edit was actually observing, and is the mechanism this pass's chip fix now also benefits from.
